exposure: internal podalic version for delivery of high floating head during cesarean section
outcome: time required for delivery of baby
cohort: The study included 150 patients undergoing elective cesarean section who were found to have a high floating fetal head, randomly distributed into three groups of 50 each.
finding: Internal podalic version for delivery of a high floating head during cesarean section was found to be a safe and rapid technique associated with fewer maternal and neonatal complications compared to forceps or vacuum delivery.
mod_finding: Internal podalic version required significantly less time for delivery and resulted in fewer intraoperative maternal complications compared to short curved forceps and vacuum delivery, with minor postoperative neonatal complications.
